proposals.statement:
theorem leftDiagonal_period_le_of_white_count (m q N n : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (w : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hw0 : w 0 = 0) (hmono : ∀ i, w i ≤ w (i + 1))
    (hstep : ∀ i < n, (∀ J, ∃ j ≥ J, leftDiagonal (m + 1 + i) j = true) ∨ w i < w (i + 1))
    (h0 : PeriodicFrom (leftDiagonal m) q N)
    (h1 : PeriodicFrom (leftDiagonal (m + 1)) q N) :
    ∃ M, PeriodicFrom (leftDiagonal (m + n)) (2 ^ w n * q) M ∧
      PeriodicFrom (leftDiagonal (m + n + 1)) (2 ^ w n * q) M := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: The period wall's residual in the form the board's own closed lemmas already reduce it to, and the first node that states the object four independent routes converged on (crystals 55-60). Carry a pair of neighbouring diagonals with a shared period q. One diagonal further in, leftDiagonal_step_period_dichotomy says either the period survives unchanged, or the middle diagonal is white for ever; and in that second case leftDiagonal_periodicFrom_step says the period at most doubles. So the period of diagonal m+n is q multiplied by two once per eventually-white diagonal passed, and by nothing else. The counter w is any nondecreasing function that ticks at each of those, so 2 ^ w n * q is the bound. This is the same induction and the same cited lemma as the closed leftDiagonal_period_le_of_black_between, which is exactly the w = 0 case: there the hypothesis forbids white diagonals outright, here they are permitted and paid for. A proof of leftDiagonal_period_le would cite this and then have only the counting claim left — that at most log2 (k+1) of the first k diagonals are eventually white — which is what that wall's own note says remains after the reduction half was split off. Measured on the packed row model, explorer/seed_whitegaps.mjs, k ≤ 400 from 3000 indices: the pair period max(period k, period k+1) is monotone in k, increases exactly at k = 2, 7, 28, 399, and those are exactly the eventually-white diagonals in range; at every k it equals 2 ^ (number of eventually-white diagonals below k+1), so the bound is attained rather than merely respected.
proposals.disclaims: Proves nothing about how many diagonals are eventually white, which is the whole of what is open. With w counting every diagonal it degenerates to the already-proved 2 ^ k. It is a claim about the left edge of the cone and bears on no prize conjecture.

proposals.statement:
theorem leftDiagonal_step_of_white_parity (m q N : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q)
    (h0 : PeriodicFrom (leftDiagonal m) q N)
    (hwhite : ∀ j ≥ N + 1, leftDiagonal (m + 1) j = false) :
    (Even (∑ j ∈ Finset.range q, if leftDiagonal m (N + j + 2) = true then 1 else 0) →
        PeriodicFrom (leftDiagonal (m + 2)) q N) ∧
      (Odd (∑ j ∈ Finset.range q, if leftDiagonal m (N + j + 2) = true then 1 else 0) →
        ∀ n ≥ N, leftDiagonal (m + 2) (n + q) = !leftDiagonal (m + 2) n) := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: Rowland (2006) Proposition 2 and Lemma 3 on the left edge — the half of the doubling criterion the board does not have. It has the other half: leftDiagonal_step_period_dichotomy says a doubling requires an eventually-white predecessor. This says what happens once you are past one. With diagonal m+1 white from N+1 on, leftDiagonal_recurrence loses its `||` term and diagonal m+2 becomes a running XOR of diagonal m: x (i+1) = x i ^^ leftDiagonal m (i+2). One period of that driver therefore flips x exactly when the period holds an odd number of black cells — even parity leaves the period at q, odd parity makes the diagonal antiperiodic, so its period is exactly 2q and not q. This is the same argument as the closed rightDiagonal_periodicFrom_step_of_even_driver and rightDiagonal_antiperiodic_of_odd_driver, read on the other edge, and h1 is not needed because whiteness supplies the middle diagonal's periodicity itself. A proof of leftDiagonal_period_le cites it to say which white diagonals actually double, turning leftDiagonal_period_le_of_white_count's `at most one doubling per white diagonal` into the exact count. Checked: the running-XOR identity leftDiagonal (m+2) (n+q) = leftDiagonal (m+2) n ^^ (parity of the window) holds on all 11,200 instances at every eventually-white diagonal below 420, every q from 1 to 64 and 400 starting points each (explorer/seed_parity.mjs). That check exists for the index alignment N + j + 2, which is the one thing here that can silently be off by one.
proposals.disclaims: On the seed the even branch is so far vacuous: all four eventually-white diagonals below 400 carry odd parity and every one of them doubles the period. So this does not on its own make doublings rarer than whites — it says the two coincide exactly when the parity is odd, and pins the period exactly in that case. Not a prize conjecture; a claim about the left edge only.

witness.range: n < 10, i.e. the instance m = 1, q = 1, N = 0 of the odd branch: diagonal 2 is white everywhere, diagonal 1 is constantly black so the one-term parity sum is odd, and the conclusion is that diagonal 3 alternates. Reads evolve to depth 13. Only this one instance; the even branch cannot be witnessed because no instance of it occurs in the seed within reach.

proposals.statement:
theorem leftDiagonal_onset_le_of_black_ladder (N : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hmono : ∀ k, N k < N (k + 1))
    (hwitness : ∀ k, leftDiagonal (k + 1) (N (k + 1)) = true ∨
        ∀ j ≥ N k + 1, leftDiagonal (k + 1) j = false)
    (k : ℕ) : ∃ p > 0, PeriodicFrom (leftDiagonal k) p (N k) := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: The onset wall reduced to one sequence of witnesses, which is the shape eleven attempts on that wall kept rebuilding from scratch. Hand over, for each diagonal, an index N (k+1) — strictly increasing, so it grows by at least one per diagonal — at which diagonal k+1 is black, or else a certificate that diagonal k+1 is white from N k + 1 on for good. Then diagonal k has already settled by N k. The black branch is leftDiagonal_periodicFrom_step_of_black, which resets the next diagonal at that black cell with the period unchanged; the white branch is the first arm of leftDiagonal_step_onset_dichotomy, which costs one index and doubles the period, and the second arm is impossible because it produces a black cell past N k + 1. leftDiagonal_onset_le then follows from a ladder with N k ≤ k. This is what crystal 45 calls `iterating it bounds the onset by the sum of the first-black gaps`, stated as a theorem instead of as a remark, and it is a genuine advance on the closed leftDiagonal_onset_le_of_line: that node's onset is pinned to the line N k = k and its second disjunct is a return condition, where this takes an arbitrary ladder and a whiteness condition — the same eventually-white object leftDiagonal_period_le_of_white_count counts. The route below compiles, exit 0, no sorry: explorer/seed_scratch_ladder.lean. Measured (explorer/seed_gapgrowth.mjs): the greedy ladder that always takes the next black cell reaches N k / k = 2.000 by k = 2000, so this reduction cannot on its own beat onset ≤ 2k, and the truth is about 0.34 k.
proposals.disclaims: Says nothing about whether such a ladder with N k ≤ k exists — that is the wall. Do not read the measured N k / k → 2 as a proof of anything: the greedy ladder cannot retreat and the real seam does, on about a quarter of rows (crystal 52). Not a prize conjecture; the left edge only.

route.tactics:
have d0 : ∀ j, leftDiagonal 0 j = true := by
    intro j; simpa [leftDiagonal] using evolve_left_edge j
  have d1 : ∀ j, leftDiagonal 1 j = true := by
    intro j; exact evolve_left_second_diagonal j
  have weaken : ∀ (f : ℕ → Bool) (p a b : ℕ), a ≤ b → PeriodicFrom f p a → PeriodicFrom f p b := by
    intro f p a b hab h n hn; exact h n (le_trans hab hn)
  have key : ∀ k, ∃ p, 0 < p ∧ PeriodicFrom (leftDiagonal k) p (N k) ∧
      PeriodicFrom (leftDiagonal (k + 1)) p (N k) := by
    intro k
    induction k with
    | zero =>
      exact ⟨1, one_pos, fun n _ => by rw [d0, d0], fun n _ => by rw [d1, d1]⟩
    | succ k ih =>
      obtain ⟨p, hp, ha, hb⟩ := ih
      have hlt := hmono k
      rcases hwitness k with hblack | hwhite
      · obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ : ∃ j, N (k + 1) = j + 1 ∧ N k ≤ j :=
          ⟨N (k + 1) - 1, by omega, by omega⟩
        rw [hj.1] at hblack ⊢
        have hstep := leftDiagonal_periodicFrom_step_of_black k p (N k) j hj.2 ha hb hblack
        exact ⟨p, hp, weaken _ _ _ _ (by omega) hb, hstep⟩
      · rcases leftDiagonal_step_onset_dichotomy k p (N k) ha hb with h | ⟨j, hj, hjb, -⟩
        · refine ⟨2 * p, by omega, ?_, ?_⟩
          · exact weaken _ _ _ _ (le_of_lt hlt) (periodicFrom_mul _ p (N k) hb 2)
          · exact weaken _ _ _ _ (by omega) h
        · exact absurd hjb (by rw [hwhite (j + 1) (by omega)]; exact Bool.noConfusion)
  obtain ⟨p, hp, ha, -⟩ := key k
  exact ⟨p, hp, ha⟩

proposals.statement:
theorem leftDiagonal_not_both_eventually_white (k : ℕ) :
    ¬ ((∃ N, ∀ j ≥ N, leftDiagonal k j = false) ∧
        ∃ M, ∀ j ≥ M, leftDiagonal (k + 1) j = false) := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: The first structural constraint on the eventually-white diagonals — the object crystals 57 to 60 report four independent routes converging on, and which no node on the board states. No two of them are adjacent. The proof descends: leftDiagonal_shift_of_white says that past a white diagonal m+2 the diagonal m read two cells along equals diagonal m+1 read one cell along, so if m+1 is white too then m is white; the pair (m, m+1) is then in the same position one diagonal further out, and the descent ends at diagonals 0 and 1, which are constantly black (evolve_left_edge, evolve_left_second_diagonal). A proof of leftDiagonal_period_le has to bound the number of eventually-white diagonals below k, and this is the only constraint on that set anyone here has proved: it improves the trivial count k to k/2, which is nowhere near the log2 (k+1) the wall needs, but it is the first fact about the set rather than about one of its members. It is also what stops leftDiagonal_period_le_of_white_count from being read as permitting a white diagonal at every index. Verified below 400, where the eventually-white diagonals are 2, 7, 28 and 399 (explorer/seed_whitegaps.mjs). The route below compiles, exit 0, no sorry: explorer/seed_scratch_routes.lean.
proposals.disclaims: k/2 is not a useful bound and this does not pretend to be one. Not a prize conjecture; the left edge only.

route.tactics:
induction k with
  | zero =>
    rintro ⟨⟨N, hN⟩, -⟩
    have := hN N le_rfl
    have hb : leftDiagonal 0 N = true := evolve_left_edge N
    rw [hb] at this
    exact Bool.noConfusion this
  | succ m ih =>
    rintro ⟨⟨N, hN⟩, ⟨M, hM⟩⟩
    have hshift := leftDiagonal_shift_of_white m M (fun i hi => hM i hi)
    refine ih ⟨⟨max N M + 2, ?_⟩, ⟨N, hN⟩⟩
    intro j hj
    have h1 : leftDiagonal m ((j - 2) + 2) = leftDiagonal (m + 1) ((j - 2) + 1) :=
      hshift (j - 2) (by omega)
    have h2 : leftDiagonal (m + 1) ((j - 2) + 1) = false := hN _ (by omega)
    rw [show j = (j - 2) + 2 by omega, h1, h2]

proposals.statement:
theorem periodicFrom_trans_period (f : ℕ → Bool) (p q N M : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p)
    (hN : PeriodicFrom f p N) (hM : PeriodicFrom f q M) : PeriodicFrom f q N := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: A machine, harvested rather than invented: a sequence that already has one positive period from N inherits every other of its periods from N too, whatever onset that other period came with. It has now been re-proved privately inside three separate pieces of work — leftDiagonal_onset_le_iff_rowNat_return's proof note names it as the step its forward direction needs, and the parked file of the eleventh attempt on the onset wall defines it again with the comment that it is private in two closed files. Every argument that walks a ladder of diagonals has to put two periodicity facts with different onsets and different periods on a common footing, and this is the one lemma that does it; both leftDiagonal_period_le_of_white_count and leftDiagonal_onset_le_of_black_ladder above want it the moment their two branches are merged. The proof is one calc: hop forward by M periods of length p to get past M, apply the q-period there, hop back. The route below compiles, exit 0, no sorry: explorer/seed_scratch_routes.lean.
proposals.disclaims: Pure sequence bookkeeping; there is no automaton in it and it proves nothing about rule 30.

route.tactics:
intro n hn
  have hMp : M ≤ M * p := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right M hp
  have h1 := periodicFrom_mul f p N hN M (n + q) (by omega)
  have h2 := periodicFrom_mul f p N hN M n hn
  have h3 := hM (n + M * p) (by omega)
  rw [← h1, ← h2, ← h3]
  congr 1
  omega

proposals.statement:
theorem centerColumn_eq_rowNat_testBit (t : ℕ) : centerColumn t = (rowNat t).testBit t := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: The missing edge between P1's own object and the row model every recent P1 node runs on. leftDiagonal_eq_rowNat_testBit reads a diagonal off one bit of a packed row, and six closed nodes since — rowNat_mod_eq_iterate, leftDiagonal_onset_le_of_le_5000, stepMod_preperiod_le_of_le_11, step_two_mul, stepMod_iterate_two_mul, leftDiagonal_onset_le_iff_stepMod_return — are stated entirely in that model because the kernel can compute row 5000 in a second where evolve gives out near row 18. The centre column has no such edge, so no fact about it can be settled by decide at all. With this it can: read together with rowNat_mod_eq_iterate it is crystal 60's dictionary, centerColumn t is bit t of the t-th iterate of r ↦ 4r XOR (2r OR r) from 1, which states the P1 residual with no automaton in it and makes crystal 19's finite exclusions reachable the way stepMod_preperiod_le_of_le_11 was. Geometrically it is also centerColumn t = leftDiagonal t 0: the centre column is every diagonal read at index 0, where settledCenter reads the same diagonal past its onset — which is why the two agree for t < 18 and part company after. The route below compiles, exit 0, no sorry: explorer/seed_scratch_routes.lean. Checked against OEIS A051023 for t < 41 in explorer/seed_parity.mjs.
proposals.disclaims: Supply, not insight, and it does not bear on aperiodicity: it is a change of notation for the centre column, and every hard thing about that sequence survives it unchanged. It opens the door to kernel computations about the centre column, and a computed prefix is not a theorem about the limit — no rung of that ladder can close P1.

route.tactics:
have h := rowCell_eq_evolve t 0
  unfold rowCell at h
  rw [if_pos (by omega : -(t : ℤ) ≤ (0 : ℤ) ∧ (0 : ℤ) ≤ (t : ℤ))] at h
  simpa [centerColumn] using h.symm
